result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers say plainly that completion, satisfaction and a same-week quiz don't show better job performance, and both give the director clear wording tied to metrics the team likely already tracks. A explicitly plans a knowledge re-test at 1–2 weeks and again around 30 days, which B never does; B's follow-up covers only job metrics at 30/60/90 days. B is stronger on causal honesty, naming confounds such as ticket mix, tooling and seasonality, and on proportionality, with a practical tip to pull the previous cohort's numbers now. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers say plainly that completion, satisfaction and quiz scores don't show better job performance, and both give usable wording for the director. A is stronger on what 12 people with no baseline can and can't support, including confounders like ticket mix and seasonality, and it keeps the plan tight. B's explicit delayed re-test is a real advantage, but its six-step plan is somewhat heavier and its caveat about causation is thinner.
